**[t1] Alex (facilitator):** Good afternoon, Dr. Sarah. What is the core friction in your current patient intake and scheduling workflow?

**[t2] Dr. Sarah (stakeholder):** We have patients arriving for appointments only to find another clinician was double-booked in the same exam room. Our staff need to coordinate examination room occupancy so conflicts are caught immediately.

**[t3] Alex (facilitator):** How do staff currently notice when an exam room is double-booked?

**[t4] Dr. Sarah (stakeholder):** They do not until two patients collide in the hallway. I picture a giant red flashing emergency beacon right on the calendar when someone double-books, screaming at the receptionist.

**[t5] Alex (facilitator):** Aside from visual alerts, how do you handle missed appointments and no-shows?

**[t6] Dr. Sarah (stakeholder):** No-shows cost us hours every day. We should remind patients twenty-four hours before their visit so they confirm attendance or release the slot.

**[t7] Alex (facilitator):** Should the reminder frequency be higher for patients with frequent historical no-shows?

**[t8] Dr. Sarah (stakeholder):** Earlier I thought about hourly SMS alerts, but actually, scratch what I said about hourly SMS reminders. Sending an SMS every sixty minutes will just annoy patients and make them block our clinic number.

**[t9] Alex (facilitator):** Understood, so a single twenty-four-hour confirmation is preferred. What about urgent triage visits?

**[t10] Dr. Sarah (stakeholder):** Urgent care patients who walk in without an appointment must be allocated to buffer slots without displacing scheduled chronic care patients.

**[t11] Alex (facilitator):** What causes the most frustration for your medical assistants right now?

**[t12] Dr. Sarah (stakeholder):** Ugh, the endless county paperwork and outdated insurance validation portals drive our assistants crazy. We waste hours printing paper claims that get rejected for missing postal codes.

**[t13] Alex (facilitator):** That administrative overhead sounds burdensome. What about schedule adjustments during provider illness?

**[t14] Dr. Sarah (stakeholder):** When a doctor calls in sick, the clinic coordinator needs to reassign affected patient visits to available partner physicians.

**[t15] Alex (facilitator):** Could an automated system cancel and rebook those appointments autonomously?

**[t16] Dr. Sarah (stakeholder):** No, absolutely not. The scheduling system must never automatically cancel an existing appointment without explicit confirmation from clinical staff.

**[t17] Alex (facilitator):** How should patient communication feel from the patient's perspective?

**[t18] Dr. Sarah (stakeholder):** Patients should experience clear, compassionate communication rather than robotic bureaucracy.

**[t19] Alex (facilitator):** Are there specialized accessibility needs for non-English speaking patients?

**[t20] Dr. Sarah (stakeholder):** Yes, appointment notices should support the patient's preferred language, but room scheduling is the top priority.
